passages.context: The complete article, Corpus Thomisticum paragraphs [36099]-[36106], was inspected in the exact response. Corpus [36103] teaches that natural principles do not suffice to order man to beatitude beyond human nature, so God superadds the theological virtues: they have God as object, are infused by God alone, and are made known by divine revelation.
passages.notes: This article establishes the supernatural origin, object, and end of the theological virtues. It does not establish their number, their functional relations, their precedence, or their increase. No printed-Leonine collation is claimed.

passages.context: The complete article, Corpus Thomisticum paragraphs [36115]-[36122], was inspected in the exact response. Corpus [36119] places faith in the intellect with respect to supernatural credibilia apprehended in divine light, hope in the will's intending and tending toward the supernatural end as attainable, and charity in the spiritual union and conformity by which the will is transformed toward that end.
passages.notes: This article establishes the triad and these functional relations. It does not establish the twofold precedence of faith, hope, and charity, which Aquinas treats in I-II.62.4, or fully specify divine assistance as hope's formal ground. No printed-Leonine collation is claimed.

passages.context: The complete article, Corpus Thomisticum paragraphs [38711]-[38718], was inspected in the exact response. Corpus [38715] places the increase of grace and charity within grace's movement toward eternal life and concludes that this increase falls under condign merit; reply 3 says every meritorious act merits increase, but the increase is given in its proper time when the person is sufficiently disposed.
passages.notes: The article concerns merit proceeding from grace or charity already possessed. It neither makes first grace merited nor says that every meritorious act immediately increases grace. It does not address the distinct question of final perseverance, which follows in I-II.114.9. No printed-Leonine collation is claimed.
